cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Removing the restaurant roof is our only affordable way to fix the ventilation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We close. A responsible business protects its customers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain is forecast all opening week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll save a week's wages. Put that toward umbrellas; we can't afford to abandon the savings now.

mechanism: A exercises approval over a disastrous restaurant plan, converting each objection into a responsible-sounding reason to continue.
confusable: High confidence alone is not enough: the bad plan must be sold as prudent and inevitable through A control of questions and spending.
comparison: Restaurant weather risk is justified through cost savings; the charity alternative rationalizes borrowing and self-bidding after losing its only supposed bidder.
seedUse: D17-a roof and closure logic already gives A ruling and financial commands a joined status-and-disaster function.
